newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday November 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday November 21.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Prime minister Romano Prodi says he will step down if Italy fails to meet the requirements for European monetary union. Prodi also says Italy is ready to start technical talks on the re-entry of the lira into Europe's ERM, but this will take a bit of time (all).
* The government won a confidence vote in parliament on a draft law designed to allow some 250,000 previously illegal immigrants to stay in Italy (all).

* In an interview, deputy prime minister Walter Veltroni says the leftist PDS party, the largest political group in the ruling coalition, should give more support to the government (Corriere della Sera).

* In an interview, finance minister Vincenzo Visco defends the one-off 12.5 trillion lire Euro-tax, which is being heavily criticised by the employers association Confindustria and by shopkeepers. Visco says it is a "fair price for Europe" (La Repubblica).

* The European Commission may review the Euro-tax component of Italy's 1997 budget and its forecast on the Italian economy. EU Commissioner Mario Monti criticises the government's plan to partly reimburse the one-off tax saying "it makes it look like borrowing, not a measure adopted to reduce the public deficit" (all).
* Paolo Costa, economist and dean of Venice's University, is the new Public Works minister (all).
* Trade unions CGIL, CISL and UIL have called a national four-hour strike in the industry and transport sectors for December 13 (all).
* Chairman of anti-trust authority Giuliano Amato criticised oil companies and said Italian consumers received no benefits from the deregulation of the petrol market (all).

* Chairman of Banca Nazionale del Lavoro Mario Sarcinelli, who joined forces with insuring group INA to present an offer for the sale of a 60 percent stake in Banco di Napoli. He says INA would be the majority shareholder if they were to win the bid (all).
* The lira hit a three-year high against the dollar, closing under the 1,500 level in New York (all).
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
